question.problem: Given $X∼\text{Geom}(\frac{5}{8}),$ compute $P(X\ge 3)$ rounded to $4$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
If $X∼\text{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}(1-p)^{x-1}p, & x=1,2,3,… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, $X∼\text{Geom}(\frac{5}{8}),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}{(\frac{3}{8})}^{x-1}(\frac{5}{8}), & x=1,2,3… \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

There are infinitely many values of $X$ such that $X\ge 3.$ However, we can simplify the computation by using the complement instead:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 3) & =1-P(X<3)\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<3) & =P(X\in \{1,2\}) \\  & =P(X=1)+P(X=2) \\  & =f(1)+f(2) \\  & ={(\frac{3}{8})}^{0}(\frac{5}{8})+{(\frac{3}{8})}^{1}(\frac{5}{8}) \\  & ≈0.8594.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 3) & =1-P(X<3) \\  & ≈1-0.8594 \\  & =0.1406.\end{aligned}
$$
